predecessors.name: Kingdom of England
predecessors.text: England and Wales, the larger part of the union: Cliopatria's Kingdom of England row runs to 1708

predecessors.name: Kingdom of Scotland
predecessors.text: the Kingdom of Scotland, united with England by the Acts of Union 1707

successors.name: United Kingdom
successors.text: 'Great Britain was merged into the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland on 1 January 1801'

ledger.x: 1707: England and Scotland unite as the Kingdom of Great Britain.
1707: Ireland stays a separate kingdom, dependent on the new Britain.
1708: Anglo-Dutch forces take Menorca from Spain.
1713: the occupation of Menorca ends in formal cession (next event).
1713: Spain cedes Menorca to Great Britain.
1713: Spain cedes Gibraltar to Great Britain at Utrecht.
1763: Menorca returns to Britain by the Treaty of Paris.
1794: British forces begin the siege of Calvi.
1794: Corsica becomes the Anglo-Corsican Kingdom under the British crown.
10 August 1794: the siege of Calvi ends (infobox 'Siege of Calvi: 17 June - 10 August 1794'); the page does not name Calvi's fall in words, so the end is the siege's end date.
4 September 1800: the French garrison surrenders and Malta passes to Britain as a protectorate.
31 December 1800: the Kingdom of Ireland ends its separate existence.

wars.name: War of the Spanish Succession
wars.outcome: British gains at Utrecht: 'From France, Great Britain gained Newfoundland and Acadia, and from Spain Gibraltar and Menorca.'

wars.name: Jacobite risings
wars.outcome: No border moved: the rising of 1715 'based in Scotland' and the cause of the Stuarts 'ended in defeat ... in 1746'.

wars.name: Seven Years' War
wars.outcome: Menorca was lost in 1756 and 'ceded back to them in the 1763 Treaty of Paris'; the Treaty of Paris of 1763 'marked the high point of the First British Empire' (Kingdom of Great Britain page).

wars.name: American Revolutionary War
wars.outcome: Menorca was captured in 1782 and ceded to Spain by the 1783 Peace of Paris; the colonies are the American dossiers' matter.

wars.name: French Revolutionary Wars
wars.outcome: Britain held Corsica as a client (June 1794 - 11 October 1796), landed on Elba (1796), retook Menorca (1798) and took Malta (4 September 1800).

certainty.note: The coast of Great Britain and the Anglo-Scottish line are long fixed; the outposts (Gibraltar by the Utrecht cession, Menorca, Malta) are small enclaves.
